report.summary: On every broker connect the panel now asks each TRV and air-sensor topic for its current state (empty publish, zigbee2mqtt replies with the full payload), so the cards fill at boot instead of waiting for a change. Builds at 2.94 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: You're right that nothing was asking for the current values: on connect the panel only subscribed, and zigbee2mqtt publishes a device topic on change only — so the cards stayed empty until a valve moved. It now requests each topic's state as part of the connect sequence, which is how Home Assistant itself fills in on restart.

The request is an empty publish to the device's own state topic, which zigbee2mqtt answers with the full state payload (the same JSON current_heating_setpoint / local_temperature / system_mode / temperature already come from) — no second topic, no extra parsing, and the air-sensor topics are polled the same way when they are set.

It runs on every (re)connect, not just boot, so a broker restart or a Wi-Fi dip also refills the cards instead of waiting for the next change. Subscribes and polls count separately in the log, so a room whose topic never fired is visible at boot.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2cd180 (2937216 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; check_code clean

findingsAddressed.finding: user report — device does not request the current values at boot; TRV/sensor topics only broadcast on change
findingsAddressed.fix: heating_broker_ready() now subscribes and then publishes an empty message to every configured TRV and air-sensor topic (zigbee2mqtt replies with the full state payload); logged as "subscribed to N room topic(s); requested fresh state of M"

openQuestions: zigbee2mqtt's reply arrives on the same topic the panel subscribed to; if a household disables that behaviour in z2m, the cards fall back to the saved targets until a change is published — no harm, just the old behaviour.
